name: two per-period count columns in one view each count their own periods (executed-result parity)
description: Two count columns whose scans differ materialize two period CTEs at (subject, period_key, year) grain, which is FINER than the outer row -- so joining them directly cross-multiplies. One player with three receiving games and three rushing games produced nine outer rows before the per-period summary landed. This fixture pins the VALUES across that change: the counts are 2 and 2 either way, because COUNT(DISTINCT period_key) is immune to uniform replication, which is exactly why a value fixture cannot be the gate on the fan-out itself -- test/data-views.per-period-summary.spec.mjs asserts the SHAPE. What this fixture does catch is the summary reducing to the wrong grain or filtering with the wrong threshold: the two columns carry DIFFERENT thresholds over the same three periods, so a summary that collapsed them onto one column, or dropped a threshold, answers 3 or answers the other column's number.
